description: Topic index for the ESSCE 2018 General Knowledge paper (gk-2018-matric). No textbook – topics follow a general-knowledge hierarchy (tools/lib/gk_topics.py); refs are general sources.

topics.title: Eritrea – geography, history, society and institutions
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Know Eritrea's six zobas (Maekel, Debub, Anseba, Gash-Barka, Northern Red Sea, Southern Red Sea), its landforms and climate zones, main towns, historical sites, languages, national symbols and institutions.

subtopics.title: Physical geography, zobas and towns
subtopics.concept: Highlands (Maekel, Debub, parts of Anseba), western lowlands (Gash-Barka), eastern escarpment (Nefasit, Ghinda) and the coastal plain/Danakil depression (Southern Red Sea – the hottest and lowest part). Only Maekel borders no foreign country.

textbook_refs.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Danakil Plain; Eritrea climate
Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea (land: Mount Soira, 9,885 ft / 3,013–3,018 m)
Administrative map of Eritrea (UN OCHA Eritrea reference map)
Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – reports on Kerkebet dam and the Kerkebet area (2018, 2020)
CIA World Factbook – Eritrea (lowest point: Near Kulul within the Danakil Depression −75 m)
Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea: relief and towns

subtopics.title: Historical and archaeological sites
subtopics.concept: Ancient sites: Qohaito, Metera, Adulis, Keskese, Belew Kelew; Asmara's modernist architecture became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2017.

textbook_refs.reference: National Museum of Eritrea / Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – archaeological sites; shabait.com 2011 ‘Mai-Dima town registers marked growth’
UNESCO World Heritage Centre – ‘Asmara: A Modernist African City’ (inscribed 2017)

subtopics.title: Languages, culture and national symbols
subtopics.concept: Nine ethnic languages; Tigrinya and Tigre use the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) script, Kunama and Bilen commonly use the Latin script, Arabic its own script. National emblem: the camel.

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrean cultural practice (shabait.com features on highland wedding season); Eritrean Orthodox Tewahdo calendar
Government of Eritrea public-holiday list (shabait.com); Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – May Day

Government of Eritrea – national symbols (shabait.com); Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – flag of Eritrea

subtopics.title: Education and public institutions
subtopics.concept: Higher-education colleges (EIT Mai Nefhi, CASS/CBE at Adi Keih, Hamelmalo, Halhale, Orotta, Asmara College of Health Sciences), school system (pre-school at 4–5, elementary 1–5, middle 6–8, secondary 9–12).
keywords: College of Arts and Social Sciences

subtopics.title: Economy, agriculture and development
subtopics.concept: Farming is rain-fed and constrained by soil erosion, land degradation, poor land-use and shortages of inputs, infrastructure and markets; dams (e.g. Kerkebet) and afforestation are remedies.

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrea National Action Programme to combat desertification (Ministry of Land, Water and Environment); FAO Eritrea country profile

subtopics.title: African history and decolonisation
subtopics.concept: Ghana (1957) was the first sub-Saharan colony to gain independence from a European power; Liberia and Ethiopia were never colonies in the usual sense. Colonisers included Britain, France, Italy, Germany, Belgium, Portugal and Spain.
